title: sse-streaming-partial-json-delimiter-ordering-fixes
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: We observed several customer reports and internal regressions where streamed SSE responses could produce malformed or out-of-order partial JSON events under certain batching/flush patterns. Symptoms included: partial JSON objects split across frames, delimiter tokens ("

" / special event markers) emitted in the wrong order relative to token boundaries, and function-calling payloads occasionally delivering the 'arguments' object before the 'name' event. This broke downstream OpenAI-compatible clients and the TS/Python SDKs that expect deterministic SSE framing.

This PR fixes the framing/token ordering issues by introducing a small deterministic state machine in the SSE frame emitter and consolidating the delimiter emission logic in one place. Key points: 1) Ensure delimiter/event tokens are emitted only after the last token chunk for an event has been flushed. 2) Preserve token-level ordering when streaming multi-part JSON (partial JSON + trailing delimiter). 3) Add adapter-level fixes in the openai-compat layer so function-calling streams present events in the same ordering as OpenAI (event: "name" then "arguments", then "done"). 4) Add comprehensive unit & integration tests that cover interleaved chunking scenarios, high-throughput batching, and backpressure-induced flushes.

What I changed: (high-level) - runtime/streaming: added a small framing state machine and a single emitter entrypoint to avoid duplicated delimiter logic. - openai-compat adapter: reorder event emission to match OpenAI ordering and ensure atomic event flush for function-calling payloads. - tests: new deterministic tests for partial JSON streaming, property-tests for token/event ordering, and an end-to-end QA harness that simulates slow client reads. - docs: updated streaming compatibility notes and added a short migration note for private deployers.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added for frame emitter (runtime) - [x] Integration tests added for openai-compat streaming - [x] Manual QA: validated against Python SDK v0.14 and TS SDK v0.9 - [x] Added release note entry - [x] No breaking API changes

Migration notes: The change is backward compatible. Private deployers running older on-host runtimes should upgrade both runtime and openai-compat adapter together to avoid mixed-behavior during rolling upgrades. See the added doc section for a recommended rolling upgrade plan.

Related: ENG-4123 (bug triage), SUP-7881 (customer incident), ENG-4210 (e2e streaming test coverage).

review_comments: Samir Gupta: Left a couple of nits on the state machine naming and one suggestion to collapse two small buffers into a single arena to reduce mempressure. Can you add a short comment describing the invariant that delimiter emission depends on?

Asha Patel: Thanks — addressed the naming and added the invariant comment. Collapsed the buffers and added a benchmark to ensure no regression in peak memory; numbers look good (<=2% increase under extreme batching).
Lina Chen: Verified tests locally and confirmed python-sdk E2E passes. Please add a short note in streaming_compatibility.md about rolling upgrade guidance for private installers.
Evan Morales: Approved after verifying that CI flaky test (streaming/timeout) was fixed by introducing the deterministic flush in the harness.
files_touched_summary: Key runtime change: frame_emitter.rs centralizes delimiting logic and adds a 3-state machine (Collecting, Emitting, Finalizing). openai-compat: streaming_adapter.py adjusts event sequencing and ensures atomic writes to the SSE socket. Tests: property tests simulate arbitrary token chunk boundaries and assert event ordering invariants.
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming chunking and framing fixes to prevent partial JSON delimiter mis-ordering, improving OpenAI compatibility and stability for function-calling streams. No breaking changes.
qa_steps: 1) Run redwood/tests/streaming locally with race=10 and ensure no failures. 2) Deploy runtime and openai-compat adapter to staging, run SDK E2E (Python/TS) and validate sample function-calling streams. 3) Smoke test high-throughput SSE client and validate well-formed JSON delivered in-order.
notes: Observed one flaky CI job historically tied to the slow-client harness; added a deterministic harness and stabilized the test. Monitor streaming_events metric for elevated framing_retries during the next 48 hours post-deploy.
